How to Clean a Smelly Kitchen Sink and Garbage Disposal

A kitchen sink can smell even when it looks clean. Food particles can collect around the drain, disposer splash guard, sink overflow opening, or plumbing trap. Greasy residue can also cling to surfaces and become noticeable as the sink warms up.

The Quick Answer

Start by physically cleaning the sink basin, drain area, and garbage-disposal splash guard. Scrub with dish soap and a non-scratch sponge, rinse thoroughly, and dry. If the disposal has a manufacturer-approved cleaning procedure, follow it instead of improvising with chemicals.

Materials Needed

- Dish soap
- Non-scratch sponge
- Old soft toothbrush or small cleaning brush
- Microfiber cloth
- Warm water
- Gloves if desired

Step-by-Step Instructions

1. Empty and rinse the sink
Remove dishes, food scraps, and standing water. Rinse the basin with warm water.

2. Scrub the basin
Use dish soap and a non-scratch sponge around the walls, drain opening, corners, and faucet base. Rinse well.

3. Clean the disposer splash guard
If your sink has a garbage disposal, turn it off and follow the manufacturer's safety instructions. Clean the accessible splash-guard area with a brush or cloth rather than reaching into the disposal.

4. Flush with water
Run water according to the disposal manufacturer's normal operating instructions. Avoid putting hands or tools into the disposal.

5. Dry the sink
Wipe the basin and surrounding counter dry. Moisture and residue make odors more likely to return.

What NOT to Do

- Never put your hand into a garbage disposal.
- Never combine bleach, drain cleaner, acids, or other household chemicals in the sink.
- Do not assume citrus peels are safe for every disposal or plumbing system.
- Do not use boiling water unless the plumbing and disposal manufacturer permits it.

US Home Tips Generic Guides Miss

Many US kitchens have garbage disposals, but the disposal is only one possible odor source. Check the splash guard and drain area before blaming the appliance. In rental homes, avoid taking apart plumbing or a disposal unless the lease and property manager permit it. If odor persists after cleaning, a plumbing issue may need professional attention.

Maintenance Tips

Rinse food residue promptly, clean the splash guard regularly, wipe the sink dry at night, and avoid letting greasy scraps sit in the drain.

FAQ

Why does my sink smell after cleaning?
The odor source may be underneath the splash guard, inside the drain area, or in the plumbing trap rather than on the visible basin.

Can I pour bleach into a garbage disposal?
Do not improvise with bleach. Follow the appliance and cleaner labels, and never mix bleach with other cleaning chemicals.

When should I call a plumber?
Persistent sewage-like odors, slow drainage, recurring backups, or leaks can indicate a plumbing problem rather than ordinary surface dirt.
